content:
Hi everyone — it's Lexa, a PhD student working on AI at NUS. I run a project called
Omega Institute with Haobo Ma, the CEO of ChronoAI — really just the two of us, betting
early on AI-driven mathematics. We've been at it for about a year, at
github.com/the-omega-institute.

The idea we started from: formalize mathematics in Lean, lay the derivations out as a
dependency graph, and then look across that graph for relationships worth checking —
implications, bridges between areas, coincidences. Something like that only works if
everything in it is machine-checkable, which is how we ended up in Lean rather than on
paper.

We have tried this three ways, and each one was a reaction to what the previous one taught
us. The first, automath, builds on top of Mathlib and leans on everything already there.
The second, newmath, asks what happens if you refuse that and rebuild from first
principles instead, with no axioms and no sorry — which turned out to be far more work
than we expected, and taught us how much of the value was in Mathlib rather than in our
engine. The third and current one, trureturing, came from noticing that our real problem
was not proving things but keeping honest track of what had actually been verified: results
are frozen into an append-only ledger, and only frozen layers can be built on.

That last strand is what brings me here. Our constructive analysis work is mathlib-free,
and we were pushing to see how far an empty axiom set could go rather than the usual
propext / Quot.sound footprint. Working on it got me interested in abstract rewriting.

I've just opened my first PR, #42293, adding Newman's lemma and the two normal-form
corollaries to Logic/Relation.lean. church_rosser is already in that file, but it
assumes the one-step diamond condition and makes no termination assumption, so neither
result implies the other.

One thing I would genuinely like an opinion on: I placed the new results next to
church_rosser, which costs one extra import (Mathlib.Logic.ExistsUnique, needed for
∃!). If people would rather keep Relation.lean free of that import, a separate
Mathlib/Logic/Relation/Confluence.lean would be easy to do instead.

The PR was written with AI assistance and I have disclosed that in the description.

Glad to be here.
